kjv: wherefore do ye tempt the LORD?
note: nissah means to test or put to the proof. Today "tempt" means to entice to sin. Same in v. 7.
wayyachalosh means he defeated or disabled them. "Discomfited" now means made uneasy.

kjv: Because the LORD hath sworn that the LORD will have war
mine: A hand upon the banner of Yah! Yahweh will have war
note: yad 'al-kes yah is obscure: "kes" is not a known word; it is read as a short form of kisse' "throne" (the KJV, following the Targum, takes "hand upon the throne" as an oath) or as nes "banner". Context decides for "banner": v.15 names the altar Yahweh-nissi, "Yahweh is my banner", and Moses' raised hands (17:11-12) are the rallying sign of the battle. Context: A hand upon the banner of Yah (medium confidence). 17:15 names the altar Yahweh-nissi 'Yahweh is my banner'; Moses' raised hands (17:11-12) were the sign of the battle. 'kes' is not otherwise a word for throne.
